edit.description: Add mergeFailures.length>0 && shippedTags.length===0 to the per-tick errored check (~L3381-3388) alongside the existing provisionFailures leg, per spec/loop.md's 'non-zero iff at least one tick errored AND zero entries shipped'.
Cover a wave where every entry hits a merge (cherry-pick) failure, nothing ships, no gate revert/tipMove — assert the tick lands in erroredTicks and loopExitCode is non-zero.

summary: Fix superviseLoop: a merge-stage-only failure tick (ships nothing, no gate revert) never joins erroredTicks, so a run stuck on merge conflicts can exit 0

per.section: Exit codes — the run never lies to CI

tests: a tick recording only mergeFailures with zero shippedTags and no gate revert is counted in erroredTicks
loopExitCode returns non-zero for a run whose every tick fails purely at the merge stage
a tick with a mergeFailure alongside a successful ship in the same wave stays out of erroredTicks (partial success remains exit 0)
acceptance: superviseLoop counts a nothing-shipped merge-failure tick as errored, so loopExitCode is non-zero per spec/loop.md's exit-code contract
notes: Found via plan-tick audit of fa03a39 (generalized §16 backstop to merge/gate stages but left the separate errored-tick/exit-code accounting provision-only). mergeReverted only tracks afterMerge-gate reverts, not cherry-pick conflicts — that's the gap.

edit.description: Narrow check's bare catch (~L1046-1052) to ENOENT only; report other readFileSync failures loudly (non-zero, name the error) instead of 'plan/pending.json absent'. Use namespacedJoin per platform-facts.md.

readPendingLoose (~L416-419) relies on existsSync, which returns false on any stat error, not just ENOENT — distinguish and surface non-ENOENT failures rather than reading them as an empty valid pending list.
Cover check surfacing a non-ENOENT read failure loudly rather than as absent.
Cover readPendingLoose surfacing a non-ENOENT failure rather than an empty valid parse.

summary: check's pending.json read and job.ts's readPendingLoose collapse any read failure (perm-denied, long-path) to 'absent', not just ENOENT — a silent false-green
tests: check's pendingPath read distinguishes ENOENT (prints 'absent', exits 0) from another read failure (reports it, does not exit 0 silently)
readPendingLoose distinguishes ENOENT (empty valid list) from another stat/read failure
acceptance: Neither check nor readPendingLoose reads a non-ENOENT filesystem failure as file-absence; both surface it per engineering.md's 'Loud or nothing'
notes: Found via posture sweep of src/cli.ts (rotation opened this tick, prior stamp 8312b25). One root defect, two sites sharing a probe — job.ts's own doc comment: 'the one probe flume status and flume job status both call'.

edit.description: readTickVerdicts (~L450) does verdicts.slice(-n); special-case n===0 to return [] before the slice.
Cover `flume log -n 0` printing nothing and exiting 0.

summary: flume log -n 0 prints the full verdict history instead of nothing — Array.prototype.slice(-0) is slice(0) in JS
tests: flume log -n 0 prints nothing and exits 0, not the full history
acceptance: readTickVerdicts(dir, 0) returns [], and flume log -n 0 prints nothing
notes: Found via plan-tick audit of 337eec2. slice(-0) === slice(0) in JS since -0 coerces; parseMaxValue already accepts 0 as valid, so this reaches production code paths, currently untested.

edit.description: Align the escape check (~L1131-1145) with the direct-children scope list enumerates and --help documents — reject a name containing a path separator the same as an undeclared/missing note, rather than resolving nested paths.
Cover `flume friction sub/note.md`-shaped input behaving consistently with the documented direct-children scope.

summary: flume friction <name> resolves nested paths (e.g. sub/note.md) though bare list only enumerates direct children and --help says name must be direct
tests: flume friction <name> with a nested path segment is refused the same as a missing note, matching bare list's direct-children scope
acceptance: friction <name> only resolves names list would also enumerate; a nested path is refused, matching --help's stated behavior
notes: Found via plan-tick audit of accbeb5. Not a path-traversal risk (stays contained under frictionDir), but the shipped --help text overpromises a restriction the code doesn't enforce — a doc/behavior consistency gap, not a security bug.
